result.question: Even if the king gave him half his possessions, what did the man of God say he still would not do?

readings.support: I still would not go with you

readings.answer: eat bread or drink water in this place
readings.support: nor would I eat bread or drink water in this place

assessments.reason: Directly matches the text: “I still would not go with you,” where “you” is the king; “him” is an acceptable pronoun substitution.

While he also says he would not eat or drink there, the question’s “still would not” corresponds to “I still would not go with you”; the eating/drinking clause is a separate prohibition introduced by “nor would I,” not the specific action tied to “still would not.”

result.reason: The passage explicitly says, “I still would not go with you,” matching the key’s answer.
